title: Empowering Our Leadership: Sharafat Karim Explores the Future of Climate Finance
excerpt: We are proud to announce that Sharafat Karim, Co-founder of Cedar Initiative, successfully participated in the “Climate Finance Fundamentals for Youth: Bangladesh Context” training held at the Bangladesh Public…
html:
We are proud to announce that Sharafat Karim, Co-founder of Cedar Initiative, successfully participated in the “Climate Finance Fundamentals for Youth: Bangladesh Context” training held at the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC).

The intensive four-day program, organized by the Economic Relations Division (ERD) and Practical Action, brought together a select cohort of youth leaders and government officials. The training bridged the gap between global climate policy—such as the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement—and local implementation through Bangladesh’s National Adaptation Plan (NAP) 2023–2050.

“Climate finance is the engine that will drive Bangladesh’s resilient future,” said Sharafat Karim. “Understanding the mechanisms behind the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the Loss and Damage Fund allows Cedar Initiative to better align our grassroots efforts with national and global priorities.”

Through this engagement, Cedar Initiative reaffirms its commitment to being at the forefront of climate advocacy and youth-led solutions in Bangladesh.

title: Empowering the Future: Cedar Initiative Hosts CS Ed Week 2025 in Rangpur
excerpt: In a significant move toward building a technologically advanced generation, Cedar Initiative has successfully organized the Computer Science Education Week (CS Ed Week) 2025 at the JAAGO Foundation School, Rangpur.…
html:
In a significant move toward building a technologically advanced generation, Cedar Initiative has successfully organized the Computer Science Education Week (CS Ed Week) 2025 at the JAAGO Foundation School, Rangpur. The event aimed to bridge the digital divide and spark interest in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and future-tech among underprivileged yet brilliant young minds.

Fueling Curiosity in AI and Robotics

The students of JAAGO Foundation School Rangpur Branch displayed an extraordinary level of enthusiasm. The workshop moved beyond traditional learning, focusing on:

  • Artificial Intelligence (AI): Demystifying how AI works and its role in the modern world.

  • The Future Landscape: Discussing how technology will reshape careers and daily life by 2030 and beyond.

  • Hands-on Engagement: Interactive sessions that encouraged students to think critically and solve problems using computational logic.

Collaborative Synergy

This impactful event was made possible through the strategic partnership with Enhanfy Global Ltd. and Youth for NextGen, whose support was instrumental in bringing these advanced concepts to the grassroots level.

“The curiosity we witnessed today in the eyes of these students is a testament to the untapped potential of Rangpur. At Cedar Initiative, we believe that this introduction to AI is not just a lesson; it is the beginning of their journey toward leading a Smart Bangladesh.”

— Representative, Cedar Initiative.

Our Vision for a Smart Bangladesh

At Cedar Initiative, our mission is to empower the youth with the tools of tomorrow. We believe that by nurturing the curiosity of these young learners today, we are laying the foundation for a sustainable, tech-driven, and “Smart” Bangladesh.

The journey that started today at the Rangpur branch of JAAGO Foundation School will continue to expand, reaching more young minds across the country.

title: Ushnota Abhijan 2025 — Immediate Humanitarian Response to the Karail Slum Fire
excerpt: The Ushnota Abhijan 2025 (Warmth Campaign) began with school-based activism, public awareness activities, and active volunteer participation. Students and teachers from different institutions came forward with…
html:
The Ushnota Abhijan 2025 (Warmth Campaign) began with school-based activism, public awareness activities, and active volunteer participation. Students and teachers from different institutions came forward with heartfelt contributions, donating warm clothing to support underprivileged communities in Dhaka.

As part of the campaign protocol, all collected winter clothes were to be sorted, cleaned, and packaged before distribution to the city’s needy population. However, an unexpected tragedy reshaped the campaign’s immediate priorities.

On the afternoon of November 25, a devastating fire swept through Dhaka’s Karail slum, leaving nearly 1,500 families homeless within minutes. Many lost their food, clothing, and shelter, pushing them into an urgent humanitarian crisis.

In response to this emergency, Cedar Initiative held an emergency board meeting and made a swift and compassionate decision. According to this decision, all winter clothes collected during the campaign until November 27 were immediately allocated and delivered to the families affected by the Karail fire.

Through this prompt action, we were able to stand beside the affected families, offering essential support and a message of solidarity in their moment of need. The Cedar Initiative remains committed to serving vulnerable communities with empathy, responsibility, and humanity.

title: Bangladeshi Youth Shines in CICA Artificial Intelligence Art Competition 2025
excerpt: A young Bangladeshi talent, Md Shahriar Azad Evan, has brought pride to the nation by securing a top position in the CICA Artificial Intelligence Art Competition 2025, organized by the Ministry of Youth and Sports of…
html:
A young Bangladeshi talent, Md Shahriar Azad Evan, has brought pride to the nation by securing a top position in the CICA Artificial Intelligence Art Competition 2025, organized by the Ministry of Youth and Sports of the Republic of Azerbaijan under the banner of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA).

Themed “Youth Empowerment in Green and Sustainable Development Goals,” this year’s competition encouraged young artists from across Asia to creatively explore how artificial intelligence can promote sustainability and innovation. Over 260 AI-generated artworks were submitted by participants from CICA Member States, reflecting a vibrant mix of cultural diversity and shared commitment to a greener, technology-driven future.

Among the winners, Md Shahriar Azad Evan, representing the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, stood out for his artistic creativity and innovative approach to portraying sustainable development through AI-generated art. His achievement highlights the growing presence and talent of Bangladeshi youth in the field of digital creativity and environmental innovation.

CICA extended its appreciation to all participants and the international jury for their contributions to this inspiring initiative, which continues to empower youth and foster collaboration across Asia through technology and art.

title: Cedar Initiative Founder to Represent Bangladesh at CICA Youth Council
excerpt: Md Shahriar Azad Evan, the Founder of Cedar Initiative, has been invited to attend the 8th Meeting of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) Youth Council. The prestigious event…
html:
Md Shahriar Azad Evan, the Founder of Cedar Initiative, has been invited to attend the 8th Meeting of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) Youth Council. The prestigious event brings together young leaders from across Asia to foster regional dialogue, peacebuilding, and sustainable cooperation.

As the Founder of Cedar Initiative, Evan has been actively working to empower youth and communities through environmental education, leadership, and sustainable action. His participation in the CICA Youth Council represents a significant step in amplifying the voice of Bangladeshi youth on an international platform.

Speaking about the opportunity, Evan expressed, “This platform will not only allow me to represent the vision of Cedar Initiative but also highlight the potential of Bangladeshi youth in driving positive change across Asia.”

The Cedar Initiative team extends heartfelt congratulations to him for this remarkable achievement and wishes him success in representing Bangladesh and the values of youth-led sustainability at the global stage.

title: Training on Basic Understanding of Climate Change
excerpt: Overview Cedar Initiative successfully organized an online training session titled “Basic Understanding of Climate Change” on 5 November 2025 via Google Meet. The session aimed to enhance participants’ foundational…
html:
Overview

Cedar Initiative successfully organized an online training session titled “Basic Understanding of Climate Change” on 5 November 2025 via Google Meet. The session aimed to enhance participants’ foundational understanding of climate science, global and local climate change impacts, and possible adaptation and mitigation strategies.

The training brought together youth volunteers and environmental enthusiasts eager to build knowledge and take action toward sustainable development.

Session Flow

  • Host:Naimur Rahman Durjoy, Co-founder – Cedar Initiative
    Durjoy opened the session by welcoming all participants and briefly introducing the objectives of the training.

  • Facilitators:

    • Fariha S Aumi, Chair – Brighters

      • Topics Covered:Weather, Greenhouse Gases (GHG), Climate, Climate Change

      • Aumi discussed the fundamental differences between weather and climate, explained the role of greenhouse gases, and illustrated how human activities contribute to global climate change.

    • Jimran, Chief Executive Officer – MAGIC Initiative

      • Topics Covered:Climate Change Impact (Local and Global), Adaptation, Mitigation

      • Jimran focused on the global and national impacts of climate change, highlighting real-world examples from Bangladesh. He also explained practical adaptation and mitigation measures to reduce vulnerabilities and enhance community resilience.

  • Vote of Thanks:Md. Shahriar Azad Evan, Founder – Cedar Initiative
    Evan concluded the session by expressing gratitude to the facilitators and participants for their active engagement and valuable contributions.

Participation

Over 37 participants joined the session from various institutions and organizations. Participants actively engaged through Q&A, reflections, and discussions, demonstrating strong enthusiasm for environmental learning and youth-led climate action.

A participation attendance sheet was maintained for all attendees.

Key Takeaways

  • Enhanced understanding of basic climate concepts and their interconnections.
  • Awareness of the local and global impacts of climate change.
  • Practical knowledge of adaptation and mitigation strategies.
  • Strengthened youth network for climate education and action.

Conclusion

The training session successfully met its objective of building fundamental knowledge about climate change among youth participants. Cedar Initiative looks forward to organizing more such sessions to foster climate awareness and inspire collective action toward a sustainable future.
